newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Bank of Mongolia says tugrik "relatively stable".
newsitem.headline: Bank of Mongolia says tugrik "relatively stable".

text.p: Mongolia's central bank said on Tuesday the tugrik would remain relatively stable and the defeat of incumbent President Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat by a former communist in elections on Sunday would have little impact.
"The tugrik will fluctuate a little bit but it will be within the band," a Bank of Mongolia spokesman said, without giving details of the band.
The central bank said Sunday's presidential elections in which opposition candidate Natsagiin Bagabandi swept to victory had had no influence on the central bank's official exchange rate.
Monday's Bank of Mongolia official rate, calculated based on weekly mid-point rate of interbank market trading, in the previous week showed a 1.24 percent decline, officials said.

The official rate has been fluctuating at below 800 tugriks, or between 778.09 and 796.76 against a dollar since April 28, figures given by the bank showed. Weekly differences have ranged between 0.1 and 2.25 percent.
The central bank said the currency rate fluctuations need not be regarded as disturbing as long as they remained under five percent in terms of the weekly change.
Commercial banks said on Tuesday the rate they were offering ranged from 788 to 805 against the dollar. Rates on Monday ranged between 750 and 790 at commercial banks.
On the street, the tugrik rate on Tuesday afternoon was below 810 tugriks against the dollar, from a low of 815 during the presidential elections.
The spokesman said the central bank's announcement in the media on Monday that the tugrik was stable had strengthened the currency.
"The market has already absorbed it," the central bank spokesman said of the election results, which had been expected.
Preliminary results showed Bagabandi, candidate of the opposition Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party, had won a decisive 60.79 percent of the vote, far exceeding opinion poll forecasts.
The Bank of Mongolia said the official exchange rate was within what the bank described as normal and expected the weekly change to show a strengthening of the tugrik in the long term.
The tugrik was 693.51 against the dollar on December 31, 1996 and depreciated in March to 847.37 tugriks but strengthened again toward the end of April.
"We had problems in March, but now the rate should be stable," the spokesman said.
The fall in the exchange rate in March was related to a seasonal surge in imports after the winter, the spokesman said.
